newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies end off sharply on cash.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies end off sharply on cash.

text.p: Further weakness in cash pork prices pressured CME hog and pork belly futures to sharp closing losses with bellies falling near limit down on late fund selling, traders said.
Lean hog futures closed 0.950 to 0.050 cent per lb lower with June off most at 84.000 cents. Pork bellies finished 2.800 to 2.000 lower with July off most at 88.850 cents.

Hog futures were overbought after Thursday's sharp gains and the setback in pork product values added to losses. Packers will likely be unwilling to pay up for hogs again Monday with margins so far in the red, traders said.
"Hogs will be on the defensive next week," one trader said.

Fund liquidation was cited on the late break with Rand Financials on both sides of the market early while RBH and Dean Witter sold, traders said. Refco and Cargill Investor Services sold late with closing sell stops pushing June down to the day's low late. In hog options, Lind-Waldock bought June 86 calls early after selling June 84.550 futures, pit sources said.

Fund selling and sell stops reinforced the break in pork belly futures and kept prices near limit losses. Weakness in cash product weighed on the market all day and futures turned technically weak after falling through the 10-day moving average and slipping to two-week lows, traders said.
"Technically, we have turned down," said Bill Cipolla, pork belly trader for Iowa Grain.
Cash bellies this week fell to the mid $80s per cwt level after reaching $90 during the week, the highest August, 1996.

The declines were largely a function of softening domestic and export demand due to the lofty prices, sources said. The decline in cash prices came despite recent light hog slaughter and subsequent pork belly production, as well as a lack of bellies moving into storage ahead of the key summer bacon demand, traders noted.
USDA estimated weekly hog slaughter this week at 1.65 million head, above 1.63 million last week but below 1.80 a year ago.
Refco and R.J. O'Brien sold July late while Rand Financials bought after selling early, pit sources said.
